prerequisites: Basic knowledge of physics and mathematics

learning_outcomes.text: Know the states of aggregation of pure substances and use models to calculate their thermodynamic characteristics.
Analyze mass, energy, and entropy balances of thermodynamic processes and cycles in open and closed systems.
Know the modes of heat transfer and the key concepts and aspects of heat exchangers.
Identify, formulate, and solve heat transfer problems using established methods.
Be able to pose and solve problems with initiative and creativity, applying critical reasoning.

syllabus_topics: Energy transfer by means of heat, work, and mass
Properties of pure substances. Property tables
Heat conduction. Conduction through multiple layers
teaching_methods: Classroom presentation of concepts and problem-solving sessions
assessment_rules: Four controls are conducted: two for Thermodynamics (T1, T2) and two for Heat Transfer (TC1, TC2). The Thermodynamics grade is (T1+T2)/2, and the Heat Transfer grade is (TC1+TC2)/2. For continuous evaluation, a minimum score of 3.5 must be obtained in all individual exams (T1, T2, TC1, TC2) to be able to average. The final continuous evaluation grade is (Thermodynamics Grade + Heat Transfer Grade)/2, with both part grades needing to be 3.5 or higher, and the final average being 5 or higher. For ordinary and extraordinary calls, if only one part is passed, its grade is saved, and the student only re-exams the failed part, needing at least 3.5 to average. Students re-taking the entire exam after passing one part will lose the previously obtained grade.
